conviction_note: PGR reports monthly. July and August are already out (EPS $1.65 and $1.63), so the release adds only September and the Q3 totals. Two forces pull against each other. First, a September with no hurricane at all argues for a September combined ratio better than the roughly 92 that consensus implies, which points to an EPS beat. Second, the same quiet weather raises the odds of a second Florida excess-profits accrual, booked in September as it was in 2025 (Q3 2025 reaction -5.78%), on top of auto PIF growth that keeps slowing. The stock has sold EPS beats when growth slowed (Q2 2026: $5.67 against about $4.64, stock -9.43%). Net: p_up 47 on a 4.0% absolute move. impact_sum (-0.95) is more negative than the scaled number (-0.24) because the beat finding is shrunk by the reaction function while the scaled number carries it through p_up; the gap is about how much the Florida tail is already in the 3.76-point put skew.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $4.28-4.43, from four estimate sources that broadly agree: FactSet $4.28 (https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:221be1a54ff95:0-pgr-q3-26-earnings-eps-estimate-is-4-28-usd/), MarketBeat $4.30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-progressive-pgr-expected-to-post-quarterly-earnings-on-wednesday-2026-10-09/), Yahoo average $4.35 with a range of 3.95-4.72, and Zacks $4.43 with a Q3 combined ratio of 89.4 and NPE $21.9B (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/progressive-set-report-q3-earnings-153100342.html, 2026-10-12). July EPS $1.65 plus August $1.63 is $3.28, so the bar implies September EPS of about $1.00-1.15 and a September combined ratio of about 92 (July 86.8, August 89.3). There is no company guidance. The stock trades on PIF growth more than on EPS: the July print was -9.43% on a large EPS beat because PIF growth slowed.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest is 6.8M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 1.9 days to cover (6.3M and 3.4 days at 09-15), about 1.2% of shares out: not crowded (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/pgr/short-interest/). Baseline: 25-delta skew +3.76 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.81, event-implied move 3.42%, 5-day run-up +5.43% into the print, 20-day +1.01%, 7% below the 52-week high. Forms 4 filed 2026-10-13 are director phantom-stock dividend reinvestments, not trades. Sell-side is 8 Buy / 12 Hold / 2 Sell, average target $235.11 (MarketBeat).

findings.finding: The Atlantic season had no hurricane through all of September 2026: the longest hurricane-free stretch in about 60 years, and the first hurricane (Isaias) formed only in October. September 2024 printed a 93.4 CR when Helene hit. September 2025, also hurricane-free, ran about 87 excluding the $950M Florida charge. Consensus (Zacks Q3 CR 89.4, EPS $4.28-4.43) implies a September CR near 92 against July 86.8 and August 89.3. That leaves room for a September CR in the high 80s and a Q3 EPS print around $4.5-4.7, a 3-8% beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats are not rewarded here. Q2 2026 EPS of $5.67 against about $4.64 consensus traded -9.43% on 2026-07-15 because PIF growth halved. The April 2026 print was +2.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus still implies a September CR of about 92, worse than both July and August despite no hurricane. If the quiet season were priced, Q3 estimates would sit nearer $4.6 and the skew would not be paying for downside. Quarter-end months do run higher (June 2026 was 90.0 against Q2's 87.3), which explains part of the gap.
findings.independence: Separate sources: the Artemis piece of 2026-10-08 calls Isaias the season's first hurricane (https://www.artemis.bm/news/hurricane-isaias-strengthens-cat-2-landfall-at-single-digit-billion-insured-loss-potential-forecast/), and the CR arithmetic uses PGR's own July and August releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000322/pgr202608ex99earningsrelea.htm). The August release shows only a 1.9 cat loss ratio for the month. This is a weather-to-company inference; PGR has not confirmed September cats.

findings.finding: Florida's excess-profits statute (s.627.066) tests 'any three-calendar-year period'. PGR booked $950M of policyholder credit expense in September 2025 for 2023-25 (CR 100.4 that month, stock -5.78%), cited the absence of 2025 Florida hurricanes as a driver, and recorded $1.224B for the full year 2025. The August 2026 release shows no policyholder credit expense in 2026 year to date, so with no Florida hurricane again in 2026 a catch-up accrual for 2024-26 could land in September as it did last year. That would take a large share of a roughly $1.10 September EPS bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-15: the $950M Florida charge took Q3 2025 EPS to $4.45 against about $5.05 consensus, and the stock fell 5.78% (baseline; https://theinsurer.com/ti/news/progressive-shares-close-down-6-after-950-million-florida-expense-drags-earnings-2025-10-15).
findings.why_not_priced: No preview found mentions a 2026 accrual, and the consensus CR of 89.4 does not look like it includes a $1B charge (that would add about 4.5 points to Q3). Against that, the 3.95 low end of the Yahoo range and the 3.76-point put skew may partly hold it. Big unknowns: whether the 2024-26 test nets out credits already paid, and how far 2026 Florida rate cuts (about 8% indicated) have lowered 2026 Florida profit. PGR has accrued nothing through August.
findings.independence: Separate sources: the 10-K reports 2025 policyholder credit expense of $1,224M and none in 2023-24 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/80661/000008066126000086/pgr-20251231_d2.htm). The hurricane-free 2026 season is in the WBTV source of finding 1, which shares that weather fact (here as cause of excess profit, there as cause of low cats; one fact, opposite signs, sized separately because they land on different lines). Florida rate cuts that weaken this: https://www.wkrg.com/state-regional/florida/florida-announces-significant-auto-rate-decreases-for-5-insurance-groups/amp. This is an inference; no document states a 2026 accrual.

findings.finding: Personal auto PIF growth has slowed every month: 8.8% in June, 8.4% in July (28,082K against 25,902K) and 8.1% in August (28,222K against 26,099K). Total PIF growth is 7%, NPW growth 5-6% against 8% a year ago (September 2025 NPW $7,128M, +8%), and average premium is falling, with the CPI for motor vehicle insurance -5.13% YoY in August. Total PIF rose 188K from July to August, so September (needing 40,743K to hold 7%) will likely show about 6.8% total and under 8% auto. Growth is the line that broke the stock in July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-15: PIF growth slowing to 7% from 15% drove -9.43% despite an EPS beat. The July and August monthly prints (2026-08-19, 2026-09-18) carry no cited reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the deceleration is public monthly and consensus PIF (Zacks, personal lines 39.4M) already assumes it. The unpriced part is only whether September breaks below 7% total or stabilises. A stabilisation would read positive; continued fade below trend reads negative. The +5.43% 5-day run-up suggests the market is leaning toward stabilisation.
findings.independence: Separate sources: J.D. Power/TransUnion Q2 2026 shopping fell to 12.6% (-1.0pt QoQ), a smaller pool of new business (https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/auto-motor/auto-insurance-shopping-cools-as-switching-accelerates-jd-power-data-shows-585447.aspx). The CPI decline is from a third-party write-up (https://actuary.info/insights/cpi-motor-vehicle-insurance-august-2026-first-annual-decline-since-2021-repair-costs-rising). Both are proxies; the company series is primary.

findings.finding: Commercial Lines' August loss/LAE ratio was 75.7 against 66.9 year to date, part of why the August CR rose 6.2 points. If September repeats it, the Q3 CR is pressured. Commercial is about 10% of premium and its PIF grew only 4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated reaction to commercial lines found; the CR swing in August carried no cited reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Public in the August release, but a one-month segment spike is easy to miss behind the headline. Net of the rest: personal lines are about 90% of premium and need only hold an August-like 67.8 loss ratio for this to stay small.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 3. Zacks expects 'improving commercial lines trends' (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/progressive-set-report-q3-earnings-153100342.html), which points the other way.

findings.finding: The BLS September CPI comes out at 08:30 ET on 2026-10-14, the same morning as PGR's release. The motor vehicle insurance index has fallen every month since February 2026 (-0.8% m/m and -5.13% YoY in August), so a sixth monthly decline would reinforce the softening-pricing narrative on the print day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found for PGR on a CPI day.
findings.why_not_priced: The trend is known; only the September value is new. A macro proxy, filed small.
findings.independence: Shares the CPI series with finding 3's independence line; kept separate because it resolves as a new print on the same morning. Release date: https://www.octagonai.co/markets/economics/inflation/cpi-in-september.md

baseline_tension: The negatives (a Florida accrual, slowing PIF) agree with the +3.76 put skew and are probably partly priced. The one positive (a hurricane-free September and a likely EPS beat) cuts against the skew, but this name's reaction function has sold EPS beats. The +5.4% 5-day run-up raises the bar for growth to stabilise.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): shrank the hurricane-free EPS-beat finding from +0.8 to +0.5, because Q2 2026's large EPS beat traded -9.43%.

Lesson 5 (inference and proxy sized small): shrank the Florida 2024-26 accrual finding from -1.0 to -0.7, because no document states a 2026 accrual and PGR booked nothing through August; kept it filed, with a wide range.
Lessons 5/7 (proxy; sign agrees with the skew so partly priced): shrank the PIF-deceleration finding from -0.6 to -0.5.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): commercial lines finding from -0.2 to -0.15, since personal lines are about 90% of premium.
Lesson 6 (bar): four consensus sources agree within $4.28-4.43, so no cap applied; abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged.
